case_title: State of Rajasthan v. Jamil Khan
aggravating_circumstances: Rape of a minor child, brutal murder, disposal of body in a train sack
high_court_outcome: Confirmed conviction but commuted death sentence to life imprisonment
offence_finally_established: Murder, rape, and causing death by negligence
neutral_facts: The accused, a 19-year-old man, raped and murdered a minor child under five years of age. The victim's body was secretly disposed of in a train sack. The crime was well-planned and involved extreme brutality, with the victim suffering severe injuries including vaginal tearing, hymen rupture, and ligature marks. The accused was a labourer and had consumed alcohol prior to the incident, which was considered as an indicator of premeditation. The trial court convicted the accused under sections 302, 376, and 201 of the IPC and sentenced him to death. The High Court confirmed the conviction but commuted the death sentence to life imprisonment, citing the accused's young age as a mitigating factor.
